amendments.body:
In engine.rs:272, TrimPlants adds raw plant biomass grams directly to fine_detritus_g_total: `self.state.detritus.fine_detritus_g_total += trimmed_biomass_g`. Plants have 28 mg N/g (PLANT_N_MG_PER_G_BIOMASS) while the detritus organic model gives ~138 mg N/g (at the default 0.16 N:C ratio). This creates N and C from nothing. The fix is one line — use the existing plant_detrital_mass_g conversion:
```rust
self.state.detritus.fine_detritus_g_total += plant_detrital_mass_g(trimmed_biomass_g, self.state.process_params.feed_n_to_c_ratio);
```
The correct conversion function (plant_detrital_mass_g) already exists in plant_growth.rs:397 and is used for senescence routing. TrimPlants is the only plant-to-detritus path that doesn't use it.
amendments.rationale: This is a direct mass conservation violation that the new budget framework would detect on any tick with a TrimPlants action. The fix is trivial (the conversion function already exists) and this is a player-accessible action that will be used regularly.

Same conservation-leak pattern as TrimPlants. CleanFilter is a common player action and the routing pattern exists in the codebase. Without this fix, filter cleaning silently destroys N and C, which the budget ledger would correctly report as unexplained loss.

amendments.body: In shrimp.rs:437-478, mortality() decrements shrimp counts without routing dead shrimp biomass to detritus or dissolved pools. Since the budget tracks shrimp N via shrimp_nitrogen_mg(adults_count, ...), each death causes N and C to vanish. The test_closed_system_n_conservation avoids this by setting adults_count=0 and juveniles_count=0 in active_budget_state(). Add routing of dead shrimp biomass (e.g., to fine_detritus or DON/DOC using the existing live_biomass_nitrogen_mg/live_biomass_carbon_mg helpers), OR explicitly document this as a known conservation gap with a TODO for the downstream audit bead (tanksim-6e5.3.4).
amendments.rationale: Shrimp mortality is an internal biological process in a closed system that should conserve mass. The conservation test's shrimp-free initial state masks this leak. When tanksim-6e5.3.4 (the bookkeeping audit) runs conservation tests with shrimp, this will surface as a failure.

amendments.body: Add a conservation test variant that includes a small shrimp population with non-zero mortality probability. Currently test_closed_system_n_conservation and test_closed_system_c_conservation use active_budget_state which sets adults_count=0 and juveniles_count=0, avoiding all shrimp-related biomass routing. A test with e.g. 5 adults (low enough for deterministic mortality with a known seed) would either (a) prove shrimp lifecycle is mass-conserving, or (b) document the expected magnitude of the leak with a wider tolerance and a comment explaining it's tracked as a known gap.
amendments.rationale: The acceptance criterion says 'closed-system ticks show near-zero net delta', and shrimp mortality is an internal closed-system process. Without shrimp in the test, the conservation guarantee is narrower than it appears. Even a test that documents the gap (with a comment pointing to the audit bead) is better than silently avoiding it.

payload.summary:
The budget tracking implementation is well-designed and correct for its core mission. The BudgetLedger, canonical total_nitrogen_mg/total_carbon_mg helpers, per-stage recording in engine.rs via maybe_record_stage, and the zero-cost-when-disabled pattern (Option<BudgetLedger>) all meet the acceptance criteria cleanly. The helpers correctly include all N/C pools including substrate_layers[*].nutrient_store_mg_n_total as required. The test_budget_component_labels_cover_all_element_bearing_fields test provides a compile-time-like guard against missing pools. All 7 tests pass, and the full test suite passes.

However, the new budget framework reveals three pre-existing mass conservation violations that are masked by the narrow test setup (no shrimp, no player actions): (1) TrimPlants adds raw plant grams to detritus without N/C-preserving conversion — the fix function already exists; (2) CleanFilter destroys microbe biomass without routing N/C to dissolved pools; (3) Shrimp mortality destroys biomass without routing. The first two are trivial fixes since the routing functions already exist in the codebase. The third is slightly larger and could be deferred to the downstream audit bead (tanksim-6e5.3.4).
